IRS990.ActivityOrMissionDesc: TO REPRESENT THE INTERESTS OF PROFESSIONALS IN INDUSTRIAL, OFFICE AND MIXED-USE REAL ESTATE.
IRS990.MissionDesc: Represent San Diegos commercial real estate. NAIOP San Diego provides its members with opportunities to:* Network with one another;* Affect public policy that impacts our business;* Initiate business opportunities;* Opine on market dynamics, trends and practices;* Promote giving back to the community where we work and live.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, Line 11b
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: A DRAFT OF THE FILING COPY OF FORM 990 IS REVIEWED BY THE TREASURER AND EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR FOR ACCURACY AND COMPLETION. A FILING COPY IS MADE AVAILABLE BUT NOT DISTRIBUTED TO EACH OF THE BOARD MEMBERS PRIOR TO FILING FORM 990 WITH THE IRS.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, Line 12c
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE ORGANIZATION HAS IMPLEMENTED PROCEDURES TO MONITOR AND ENFORCE COMPLIANCE WITH THE CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY. THE PROCEDURES INCLUDE ANNUAL REVIEW OF THE POLICY AT THE FIRST BOARD MEETING AS WELL AS HAVING EACH BOARD MEMBER SIGN AND RETURN A QUESTIONNAIRE STATING THE POLICY HAS BEEN REVIEWED AND NO KNOWN CONFLICTS EXIST.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, Line 15a
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE COMPENSATION OF THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR IS REVIEWED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS DURING THE BUDGETING PROCESS TO ENSURE MARKET COMPARABILITY. THE CONTRACT IS A FIXED FEE ARRANGEMENT WHEREBY THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE MAKES THE FINAL DECISION AND RESULTS ARE DOCUMENTED IN THE MEETING MINUTES.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section C, Line 19
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE ORGANIZATION MAKES ITS ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION, CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY, AND INTERNAL FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC UPON REQUEST.
